title: Income statement
examples: What is the main purpose of an income statement?
How do I calculate gross profit?
Does the income statement show cash flow?

explain.say: The income statement shows a business's profit over a period.
Revenue is the total money earned from sales of goods or services.

items: This is the top line figure

explain.say: Cost of Goods Sold, or COGS, is the direct cost of making your product.

items: Direct Material | Cost per unit | Total COGS

explain.say: Gross profit is what is left after taking COGS from revenue.
Operating expenses are costs like rent, wages, and electricity bills.
Net profit is what remains after subtracting all expenses from gross profit.

faq.q: What is the difference between revenue and profit?
faq.a: Revenue is the total money you brought in from sales. Profit is what is left after paying all your costs and expenses.
asks: Is revenue the same as income?
How do I find the actual profit amount?

faq.q: Do I need to include interest paid on a loan?
faq.a: Yes, interest paid is usually considered an expense and must be subtracted to find the final net profit.
asks: Where does interest expense go on the statement?
Should I subtract interest from gross profit?

faq.q: Does the income statement show how much cash the business has?
faq.a: No, it shows profitability over time, not the actual movement of cash. For that, you need a cash flow statement.
asks: Is profit the same as cash?
Which statement shows the bank balance?

faq.q: What if a business has no sales that period?
faq.a: If there are no sales, the revenue will be zero. You will still record any expenses that were incurred.
asks: What happens if revenue is zero?
Can a business have expenses with no sales?

faq.q: Should I list all expenses in one big group?
faq.a: It is better to group similar expenses like salaries, rent, and utilities separately for clarity.
asks: How should I categorize my costs?
Is there a standard way to list expenses?

facts: The income statement covers a period of time, like a quarter or a year.
Gross profit measures performance before overhead costs are considered.
Net profit is the final measure of the business's overall profitability.
Expenses are costs incurred to generate revenue.

quiz.say: A shop sold items for one thousand pounds and had direct material costs of three hundred pounds. What is the gross profit?
quiz.why: Gross profit is calculated by subtracting the direct costs of goods sold from the total revenue.

wrong.0: This is only the cost of the materials, not the profit.
wrong.1: You must first find the gross profit before subtracting other expenses.
wrong.3: This is only the total revenue before any costs are taken away.

quiz.say: A business has a gross profit of five thousand pounds and total operating expenses of two thousand pounds. What is the net profit?
quiz.why: Net profit is found by taking the gross profit and subtracting all the operating expenses.

wrong.0: This figure ignores the operating expenses that must be paid.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the expenses back to the gross profit figure.
wrong.3: This only records the total expenses without considering the gross profit.

quiz.say: If a company's revenue is twenty thousand pounds and its total expenses are sixteen thousand pounds, what is the net profit?
quiz.why: The net profit is the final amount remaining after subtracting all expenses from the revenue.

wrong.1: You cannot add COGS if it was not provided in the problem details.
wrong.2: This calculation is correct, but the process must show the intermediate step of gross profit.
wrong.3: This incorrectly subtracts an assumed profit figure instead of the actual expenses.
